In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the serum calcium determination has been found to be of definite value in the diagnosis of certain diseases and in the follow-up of certain patients.
the serum Ca and serum P are not as sensitive as the serum protein-bound iodine, but are more specific than that test.
the Ca and P determinations are a useful adjunctive laboratory aid in the investigation of patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca/P ratio is a more reliable index than either test alone.
the serum Ca and P values are more useful in the diagnosis of metabolic bone disease than in other diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca and P should be evaluated together.
Ca and P determinations are useful in a wide variety of diseases and that they are not only of value in the diagnosis but also in the management of the disease.
the serum inorganic phosphorus is a more sensitive and specific index of disease, and it is more sensitive than serum calcium in the detection of disease.
